subject: Re: ACME - Rate limits / Overage pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T15:10:00Z
Subject: Follow-up from today - rate limits / burst behavior

Hey Marissa,

Thanks for the call today — Rafael and Camila were really helpful walking through how Redwood handles burst traffic and quota increases. Two quick items I promised to confirm internally:

1) Typical monthly token profile: we expect ~250M tokens/month baseline, with spikes up to ~1.2B tokens during product launches (spikes last 2–6 hours). Those spikes aren’t constant — maybe 6–8 times/year.

2) Target unit economics: our finance team is modelling toward ~$18 per 1M tokens (all-in) as a target for this project.

A few questions:
- How does Redwood price short-term bursts beyond quota? Are burst tokens billed at the overage rate or are there separate burst allowances with a different unit price?
- If we commit to a 12-month reserved pool, what does the overage pricing look like for bursts above the pool? Any tiered thresholds?
- For very short, intense bursts (e.g., 2–4 hours), is there a fast quota increase process to avoid throttling, and what SLAs apply?

We’ll share the procurement spreadsheet once I get internal alignment. Can you send the rate-limits and overage pricing doc you mentioned?

Thanks,
Jordan
Product Ops, ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today - rate limits / burst behavior

Jordan — thanks for the recap and for sharing the numbers. Helpful. Quick answers inline, and attaching a short PDF that summarizes our rate-limit and overage policies.

- Baseline vs burst: Redwood treats reserved capacity (if you purchase a Dedicated/Reserved pool) separately from burst/overage. Baseline comes from your reserved pool. Bursts beyond the reserved pool are handled in three ways depending on configuration and availability:
  - Automatic burst allowance: short bursts are allowed up to a configurable percentage above the committed pool (typical defaults: 20–50%) for short windows; these are billed at the standard committed-unit rate (so no premium).
  - Overage billing: if usage exceeds both the reserved pool and the automatic burst allowance, tokens are billed at the published overage rate (we normally apply a per-1M token price that can be different from the committed rate).
  - Fallback routing: for sustained excess we route to compatible cheaper quantized variants (if you opt in) to control cost.

- Overage tiers: for committed customers we support tiered overage pricing. Example tiers in the attachment: up to 1.5x baseline = +20% unit price; 1.5–3x = +40%; >3x = custom negotiated. We can lock better band pricing with a 12‑month commit.

- Fast quota increases: we offer a rapid quota increase process for Dedicated customers. If you purchase reserved capacity, you can pre-authorize a burst policy that allows automatic temporary increases (typically 1–4x for short windows) with a 30–60 minute activation SLA. For hosted customers, we can often raise soft limits within a few hours but it depends on availability.

I attached the PDF that shows the exact numbers we quoted on-call. Rafael — tagging you to add anything on procurement/discounts.

Next steps:
1) I’ll send the formal rate-limits/overage PDF (attached).
2) Jordan to share procurement matrix and confirm target $/1M tokens (Jordan said $18/1M).
3) If ACME is comfortable, we’ll put together a 12‑month reserved proposal with burst policy and overage bands for review.

Attaching: redwood-rate-limits-and-overage-2027-03.pdf

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-23T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today - rate limits / burst behavior

Jordan — quick procurement note: we can structure the reserved pool + burst policy two ways that align with ACME's $18/1M target:

Option A (Reserved + favorable overage):
- 12-month reserved commitment: 300M tokens/month at $15/1M (committed unit rate)
- Automatic burst allowance: +30% up to 2 hours, billed at $15/1M
- Overage tiers: 1–1.5x = $18/1M, 1.5–3x = $21/1M, >3x = custom

Option B (Larger commit, lower overage):
- 12-month reserved commitment: 500M tokens/month at $13.5/1M
- Automatic burst allowance: +50% up to 4 hours, billed at $13.5/1M
- Overage tiers: 1–1.5x = $16/1M, 1.5–3x = $19/1M, >3x = custom

Both options include the pre-authorized fast quota increase option (30–60 minute activation) and a documented escalation path. If you want formal pricing with a worksheet for your procurement team, send over the spreadsheet mentioned and I’ll populate it.

Rafael
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2027-03-24T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today - rate limits / burst behavior

Thanks Marissa/Rafael — that helps a lot. I’ve attached our procurement matrix (acme-procurement-matrix.xlsx) to the internal thread here and looped in Procurement. A couple notes:

- Our finance team will evaluate the two options vs the $18/1M target — Option A looks promising from a predictability perspective; Option B might hit the target if we can commit to higher baseline.
- We’d like to include a clause for a one-time emergency top-up (manual override) with an agreed capped unit price to avoid outages during launches. Is that something Redwood can contractually guarantee for Dedicated customers?
- Please populate the DocuSign for the PO when we lock the option — sending a link in a follow-up.

Next actions: Rafael to provide a populated worksheet and a draft clause for the emergency top-up; Marissa to share final priced proposal once we confirm bands.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Jordan
Product Ops, ACME Corp
